title: Overplaying, swing and the beat; loud players in New Orleans
summary: Braud says he overplayed on early records, stresses swing and the beat, and recalls loud but polished players like Bowden and Keppard.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But you made it. Oh, well, I can fix him that out. I didn't enjoy it so well. The first records I didn't enjoy them so well because I'm overplaying. See, the method teach you to not overplay this. And if you don't go by the method, you'll go right, because the man that wrote it, he wrote it right. Well you can tell from them records, you can tell the difference. That's moving. But you see, you have a good swing drummer, you've got a good piano player, you've got the beat. Dixie Lamb is just a beat. It's like the tune Duke Gellman wrote. It don't mean a thing if you ain't got that swing. See it? It's a fine thing. I don't care how good the artist is. If you don't have the Dixie Lamb beat, he ain't there.

If there's anything else you want to hear, otherwise, anytime you want to go, we can drive back. That boy is a shock, he's a great drummer too, the one drop paid, Brunus boy. Oh yeah. That'd be Brunus. Or some drummer. I can tell you about drummers.

That kid turned New York upside down. Who's that boy from the Orleans play with Reed Allen? He's some drummer too. I don't know. He make them fellas like Cozy Cozy and them sound bad. Zooty, if that play sound bad, they make them sound awfully bad. Who is, when was this, recently? Oh, he was a drummer. That guy's a drummer.
But I don't like radio on band.
Too noisy. Well did they have loud men down here when you were young?
When you were young, did they have loud musicians down here? Oh, they had musicians loud and that, but they was polished.

Buddy Bowden, Manny Parade, loud players, Freddie Kep. But of course Freddie Kep will play his trumpet right in here and entertain you right in here by himself. It still wouldn't be too loud. It wouldn't be too loud, but when it was time to play high, he played high. Well I was born in St. James Parish, 1891.
